gaps.sentence: We should ___ an effort to arrive on time.
gaps.explanation: make an effort is the fixed collocation meaning to try hard.

gaps.sentence: It's your turn to ___ care of the dog this weekend.
gaps.explanation: take care of somebody/something means to look after them.

gaps.sentence: I'd like to ___ a suggestion, if I may.
gaps.explanation: make a suggestion is the fixed collocation; 'say a suggestion' is not used.

gaps.sentence: We ___ breakfast on the terrace every morning in summer.
gaps.explanation: have breakfast/lunch/dinner is the standard collocation for eating meals.

gaps.sentence: The referee warned the players not to ___ the rules.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'rules' (the referee warns against it)
gaps.explanation: break the rules means to disobey them; the context ('warned not to') requires this meaning.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a serious accident on his motorbike last year.
gaps.explanation: have an accident is the fixed collocation for being involved in one.

gaps.sentence: Our guide was highly ___ and had climbed the mountain five times.
gaps.explanation: highly experienced is the standard collocation; 'highly' combines with participial adjectives.

gaps.sentence: The wedding will ___ place in the village church.
gaps.explanation: take place means to happen; it is the fixed phrase for events.
